text: 🇲🇽🌎 "September is the month of the homeland — remember the origin of our country: sovereign, independent, free." Speaking in Coahuila, Sheinbaum tied her government's project to Mexico's founding: a country born sovereign and independent. In 11 days the nation marks the Grito de Independencia — Hidalgo's 1810 call in Dolores for the people to fight for freedom. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Coahuila

🇲🇽🚆 "In about three years, you'll be able to go from here all the way to Mexico City by train." Saltillo sits on the Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo and central corridors of Mexico's rail revival — 2,377 km of new passenger and freight track, double what the entire previous administration built. Passenger service starts returning between late 2026 and 2027. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Saltillo, Coahuila

🇲🇽✊ 884,942 people in Coahuila now receive a Bienestar payment — 19,223 million pesos delivered. "We defend love made policy, through the Programas de Bienestar," Sheinbaum said in Saltillo. Pensions for seniors and for women 60–64, student scholarships and disability support are now written into Mexico's Constitution as rights — not charity that can be taken away. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Saltillo, Coahuila

🇲🇽✊ "There is no divorce, no distance. We are one and the same — government and people of Mexico." At her "Honestidad y Resultados" event in Saltillo, Coahuila, Sheinbaum described the Fourth Transformation as a government fused with its people, not standing above them. Coahuila drew one of the largest crowds of her national accountability tour. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Saltillo, Coahuila

🇲🇽🌎 On the U.S. border, Sheinbaum drew the line: cooperation, yes — subordination, never. "That's what we aspire to: a good relationship with our neighbor to the north. But cooperation always, subordination never. That is the essence of us Mexicans." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León She recalled the good moments between the two nations — Juárez and Lincoln, Cárdenas and Roosevelt, AMLO and Trump's first term — as the model: cooperation between equals, on Mexico's own terms.

🇲🇽✊ When she reached the presidency, a comedian sneered that "a housewife has arrived." Her reply: "With great pride I am a housewife, a mother, a grandmother — and by the will of the people of Mexico, supreme commander of the armed forces." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León She announced a new pension for women aged 60–64 that recognizes unpaid care work. "Women can be whatever we want to be. There are no limits."

🇲🇽✊ A former president called seniors who receive the pension "a bunch of lazy people." Sheinbaum answered him. "For us, older adults are heroes and heroines of the homeland. They have given their lives to their families, their communities, their state and their country." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León Mexico is the only country where every adult over 65 receives a pension — now written into the Constitution. In Nuevo León alone, 583,000 seniors receive it.

🇲🇽✊ They said raising the minimum wage would bring inflation, kill investment, and crash the peso. The opposite happened. "The minimum wage went up — and there is record foreign direct investment, no inflation, and the peso is one of the strongest currencies in the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León In 2018 Mexico's minimum wage was 2,800 pesos a month. Today it is over 9,500 — a 154% increase in real terms.

🇲🇽⚖️ Mexico abolished slavery in 1810 — decades before the United States. "We were the first country on the continent to call for the abolition of slavery. The United States did so much later — and had a Civil War over it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León Hidalgo proclaimed the end of slavery in 1810, at the very start of the independence war. The U.S. did not abolish it until 1865, after a war that split the country.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's new-car sales top 1 million in 8 months for the first time ever</u>

Mexicans bought 1,014,832 new light vehicles from January to August 2026 — up 4.7% year-on-year and the first time domestic sales have cleared a million before September, per INEGI/AMIA data reported by El Financiero. August alone moved 129,479 units, the second-strongest August in the industry's history. A home market this strong is the flip side of the peso's best run in two years.
